II and III are correct statements.

"In a p-type semiconductor the majority carriers are electrons" is false, so I must be excluded.

The answer is II and III only.

text: Which of the following statements about semiconductors and diodes is correct? I. An n-type semiconductor is produced by doping with a pentavalent impurity II. A diode cannot be used for rectification III. A semiconductor is a better conductor than copper
explanation:
An n-type semiconductor is produced by doping with a pentavalent impurity — this is correct.

The other two statements are not true: "A semiconductor is a better conductor than copper" and "A diode cannot be used for rectification" both misstate the physics.

So only I is correct.

text: Which of the following statements about semiconductors and diodes is correct? I. The resistance of a semiconductor increases as temperature increases II. Doping reduces the conductivity of a pure semiconductor III. A diode can be used to rectify alternating current
explanation:
A diode can be used to rectify alternating current — this is correct.

The other two statements are not true: "Doping reduces the conductivity of a pure semiconductor" and "The resistance of a semiconductor increases as temperature increases" both misstate the physics.

So only III is correct.

text: Which of the following statements about semiconductors and diodes is correct? I. A diode conducts equally well in both directions II. In an n-type semiconductor the majority charge carriers are electrons III. An n-type semiconductor is produced by doping with a trivalent impurity
explanation:
In an n-type semiconductor the majority charge carriers are electrons — this is correct.

The other two statements are not true: "An n-type semiconductor is produced by doping with a trivalent impurity" and "A diode conducts equally well in both directions" both misstate the physics.

So only II is correct.

text: Which of the following statements about semiconductors and diodes are correct? I. A semiconductor has a conductivity between that of a conductor and an insulator II. A diode conducts equally well in both directions III. In a p-type semiconductor the majority charge carriers are holes
explanation:
I and III are correct statements.

"A diode conducts equally well in both directions" is false, so II must be excluded.

The answer is I and III only.
